elements.name: lai.ai-you-can-use.l09.intro
elements.html:
Make creative choices and distinguish attribution, permission, and authorship.

You can choose, combine, reject and rewrite ideas to express your own intent. Keep a record of what you made and what help you used. Attribution tells people where material came from; it does not automatically give permission to use it. In the United States, copyrightability depends on human authorship, and AI assistance does not erase protection for qualifying human contributions. Rules differ by country and the details matter; do not treat “AI-made” as a universal permission slip.

Practice scenario

You are making a fictional club poster. Options include your own drawing, an image with a clearly applicable reuse license, and a copied illustration with no permission information.

elements.name: lai.ai-you-can-use.l09.rights
elements.title: Which plan has a clearer rights basis?

choices.text: Use the unlicensed illustration and add “credit to artist.”
Use your drawing or verify the other image’s license and follow its conditions.
Assume any AI output is automatically free of every rights issue.

elements.name: lai.ai-you-can-use.l09.rights.feedback.copy
elements.html: Credit alone does not establish permission.

elements.name: lai.ai-you-can-use.l09.rights.feedback.licensed
elements.html: Check permission separately from credit and keep the record.

elements.name: lai.ai-you-can-use.l09.rights.feedback.ai
elements.html: AI involvement does not settle all rights questions.

elements.name: lai.ai-you-can-use.l09.voice
elements.title: Which revision shows your creative judgment?

choices.text: Reject a slogan that misrepresents the club and write a specific alternative.
Accept every suggestion because the model is creative.
Say no tools were used even if they were.

elements.name: lai.ai-you-can-use.l09.voice.feedback.own
elements.html: Your choice has an explained purpose.

elements.name: lai.ai-you-can-use.l09.voice.feedback.all
elements.html: That avoids evaluating whether the work represents you.

elements.name: lai.ai-you-can-use.l09.voice.feedback.claim
elements.html: Describe the process honestly where disclosure is required or useful.

elements.name: lai.ai-you-can-use.l09.transfer
elements.title: Draft a slogan and explain one idea you rejected. Add a short materials/assistance note and a rights question you would resolve before publication.
elements.description: Practice text only. Saved on this device. Reviewed by you or an educator, not AI graded.

validators.text: Add enough reasoning to review (at least 30 characters).

elements.name: lai.ai-you-can-use.l09.rubric
elements.html:
Self-check

  • Makes an original, purposeful choice.
  • Distinguishes credit from permission.
  • States assistance honestly and identifies uncertainty.

U.S. copyrightability is not a global rule or a ruling on all AI training disputes. Seek qualified guidance for a real contested publication.
